definition: To use time badly or inefficiently instead of doing something useful.
examples: I waste a lot of time playing games and messaging on my computer instead of studying. [1]

definition: To spend less time doing something than you normally would.
examples: If you take the motorway, you'll save time – it's much quicker than the local roads. [1]

definition: To do something that keeps you busy while you are waiting for something else to happen.
examples: I had three hours to wait for my flight, so I sat there doing sudoku puzzles to kill time. [1]

definition: To do something without hurrying.
examples: There's no hurry, so take your time. [1]

definition: To do something quickly or very often because you wish you had done it earlier.
examples: When my mother was young, she never had the chance to travel. Now she's retired and wants to make up for lost time, so she's booked a trip around the world. [1]

definition: To deliberately make a situation difficult for someone or criticize them.
translation: Hacer pasar un mal rato / Dar la lata
examples: I'd better go home now. If I'm late again, Dad will give me a hard time. [1]

definition: To find the time to do something, despite being busy.
examples: I would like to go camping this weekend, but my final exams are next week, so I can't spare the time. [1]

definition: To consume or occupy one's available time entirely.
examples: My children take up all my time – I never seem to get to read a book or watch a film! [1]

term: Have the time of your life
definition: To enjoy yourself very much, more than you ever have before.
translation: Pasarlo de maravilla / Vivir la mejor experiencia de tu vida
examples: New York's such a fantastic city! You're going to have the time of your life there. [1]

definition: To have no more time available to finish something.
examples: Let's not spend too long at the museum or we'll run out of time. [1]

definition: To delay making a decision or doing something in order to gain advantage.
examples: They want us to sign the contract today, but I'm not sure about it. I think we should play for time. [1]

definition: Punctual; arriving at the correct or arranged time.
examples: I'm really punctual, so I hate it when other people aren't on time. [1]

definition: Happening before you were born or before you were old enough to remember.
examples: I've never heard of that singer. He must have been before my time. [1]

definition: A period of time when you do not work due to illness or holidays.
examples: She's been working too hard recently. She needs some time off. [1]

definition: Old-fashioned in ideas, methods, or tastes.
examples: My dad's a bit behind the times – he still thinks men should wear a suit and tie at work. [1]

definition: Very quickly or very soon.
translation: En un abrir y cerrar de ojos / En un instante
examples: I thought it would take ages, but in fact I finished it in no time. [1]

definition: Having finished or arrived earlier than necessary, leaving extra time.
examples: But in the end I got to the airport with time to spare. [1]

definition: Having nothing to do; an abundance of free time.
examples: I've got time on my hands since I retired. [1]

definition: Used when you think that something will inevitably happen in the future.
examples: It's only a matter of time. [1]

definition: Taking or needing a lot of time.
examples: It's incredibly tedious and time-consuming. [1]
